profile.summary: SCimilarity is a model for searching large single-cell RNA-seq atlases for cells similar to a query cell. It takes a cell's normalised expression profile and outputs a 128-dimensional embedding in which similar cell states lie close together, so a query can be matched against a reference of 23.4 million cells, and cells can be annotated, without retraining on new studies.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.rst; paper Fig. 1 legend and Methods

summary_quotes.text: This enables a novel cell search capability, which sifts through millions of profiles to find cells similar to a query cell state
a query cell profile is compared to a searchable reference foundation model of 23.4 million profiles from 412 studies
The 128-dimensional outputs are unit length normalized
generalizes to represent new studies without additional training

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: A fully connected encoder reduces 28,231 genes through hidden layers of 1,024, 1,024, 1,024 and 128 units; the 128-dimensional output is scaled to unit length, so embeddings lie on a hypersphere. Training combines a triplet loss, which uses Cell Ontology annotations to pull cells of the same type together and push different types apart, with a mean squared error reconstruction loss from a decoder that preserves finer variation. Training uses heavy dropout (40% on the input, 50% on hidden layers).

quotes.text: starting from 28,231 genes through four hidden layers with dimensions 1,024, 1,024, 1,024 and 128
forcing all low-dimensional cell representations to lie on the surface of a hypersphere
cell triplets are sampled, each consisting of an anchor cell
an unsupervised mean squared error (MSE) reconstruction loss function, which encourages the model to preserve variation from the input expression profiles
the input layer is subjected to 40% dropout
each hidden layer is subjected to 50% dropout rates

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The pretrained model is distributed on Zenodo as model_v1.1.tar.gz (record version 1.1), which bundles model weights, embeddings, kNN graphs and metadata; Zenodo says it is meant for SCimilarity API v0.2.0. The tutorial's text links a different Zenodo record (8240464) while its download command uses record 10685499. A result should name model v1.1 and the API version.

quotes.text: This release of the model is intended for use with v0.2.0 of the SCimilarity API.

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: Searching public atlases for cells similar to a query state, cell type annotation and integrating datasets, all from embeddings computed without retraining.

quotes.text: allows researchers to quickly and systematically leverage massive public scRNA-seq atlases to learn about a cell state of interest
This tutorial is to familiarize users with SCimilarity's basic cell annotation functionality.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Metric-learning cell embedding model for cell search and annotation, trained with cell-type labels.

quotes.text: metric learning could provide a meaningful metric for the similarity between cells

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Fully connected encoder (28,231 genes to 1,024, 1,024, 1,024 and 128 units) with a decoder for reconstruction; triplet plus MSE losses.

quotes.text: The SCimilarity model consists of one fully connected encoder and one decoder stage
starting from 28,231 genes through four hidden layers with dimensions 1,024, 1,024, 1,024 and 128

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Single-cell counts aligned to the model's fixed gene order and normalised as log tp10k.

quotes.text: It is important to match Scimilarity's normalization so that the data matches the lognorm tp10k procedure used during model training.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: 128-dimensional unit-length cell embeddings; cell type annotations and nearest-neighbour search results from the bundled reference.

quotes.text: The 128-dimensional outputs are unit length normalized

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not stated as a count in the sources read; the layer sizes are given.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Training set: 7,886,247 single-cell profiles from 56 studies (46 scRNA-seq and 10 snRNA-seq) with 203 Cell Ontology author-annotated terms; 15 further datasets were held out for testing. The searchable reference, which is not the training set, holds 23.4 million profiles from 412 studies.

quotes.text: We trained SCimilarity models with a training set of 7,886,247 single-cell profiles from 56 studies (46 scRNA-seq and 10 snRNA-seq) with 203 Cell Ontology author-annotated terms
56 training and 15 test datasets with Cell Ontology annotations from across the body are used as input

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not stated as a date. The paper describes study growth between December 2018 and March 2021 when motivating the corpus.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 28,231 input genes in a fixed order; genes not in the model's list are dropped and missing ones zero-filled.

quotes.text: Genes that are not present in the new data will be zero filled to comply to the expected structure.

steps.title: Install
steps.explanation: Installs the latest API release from PyPI; the model release is intended for API v0.2.0.

quotes.text: This release of the model is intended for use with v0.2.0 of the SCimilarity API.

steps.title: Download model and data
steps.explanation: The tutorial's commented download commands, uncommented. The tutorial expects the model unpacked at /models/model_v1.1; run tar inside /models or adjust model_path.

steps.title: Embed cells
steps.shell:
python - <<'EOF'
import scanpy as sc
from scimilarity import CellAnnotation
from scimilarity.utils import align_dataset, lognorm_counts

model_path = "/models/model_v1.1"
ca = CellAnnotation(model_path=model_path)
data_path = "/data/GSE136831_subsample.h5ad"
adams = sc.read(data_path)
adams = align_dataset(adams, ca.gene_order)
adams = lognorm_counts(adams)
adams.obsm["X_scimilarity"] = ca.get_embeddings(adams.X)
EOF
